 Jitender Kumar & Ors.
Govt Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr.
Coram:

Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Vikas Mahajan
 
% 31.05.2023 Crl.M.A. 15497/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking quashing of FIR No. 374/2020 under Sections 498A/406/506/323/34 IPC registered at P.S. Badarpur, Delhi alongwith all other proceedings emanating therefrom, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
4. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
She submits that since the aforesaid FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute and the parties have arrived at a settlement, the State has no objection in case the This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/10/2023 at 07:36:40 FIR in question is quashed.
5. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 19.11.2018 according to Hindu Rights and Customs.
Out of the said wedlock, no child was born.
6. On account of temperamental differences, the parties started living separately w.e.f. 02.11.2019.

sentences.text:
During the pendency of the proceedings, the matter was referred to Counselling Cell, Saket Court,
New Delhi, where the settlement was arrived at between the parties, the terms of which were recorded in writing on 13.12.2022.
8. In terms of the said settlement, it was agreed between the parties that they will get their marriage dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

9. In terms of the said settlement, the parties have also obtained a decree of divorce by mutual consent dated 04.03.2023.
10.

It was also agreed between the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 that the petitioner no. 1 shall pay a total amount of Rs. 8,50,000/- to respondent no. 2 towards full and final settlement of her claims on account of Stree Dhan, maintenance (past, present and future), permanent alimony etc. in three instalments.

11. Out of the settlement amount, the petitioner no. 1 has already paid an amount of Rs. 6,00,000/-
at the stages mentioned in the settlement agreement, the receipt of which the respondent no. 2 acknowledges.

The balance amount of Rs. 2,50,000/- has been paid by the petitioner no. 1 to respondent no. 2 in the court today by way of demand draft no. 387707 dated 26.05.2023 drawn on Punjab National Bankm, Johri Pur, Shiv Vihar,
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/10/2023 at 07:36:40 Delhi 110094.
12.
The respondent no. 2 who is present in court submits that she has no objection in case the aforesaid FIR is quashed.
13. In view of the facts that the parties have arrived at a settlement, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
14. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and the proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.

15. Consequently, the petition is allowed and FIR No. 374/2020 under Sections 498A/406/506/323/34 IPC registered at P.S. Badarpur, Delhi alongwith all other proceedings emanating therefrom, is quashed.
16. The petition is disposed of.
17. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 31, 2023 N.S. ASWAL
This is a digitally signed order.
